candidates.title: The Coordination Tax and the Heterogeneity Dividend: Break-Even Conditions for Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
candidates.citationVelocity: published 7 days; Semantic Scholar 429 rate-limited on 2 retries, inferred near-certain 0 citations given recency
candidates.institution: Andreas Zettl, Diego Gosmar; VoiceInteroperability.ai / Linux Foundation AI & Data (Open Voice Interoperability Initiative working group)
communitySignals: Picked up by GitHub curation list chen742/Awesome_multi-agent-system issue #27 (2026-10-30)
no HF Daily Papers / Papers with Code entry located
credibilityEvidence: Full text read: closed-form coordination-tax model (decomposition inflation alpha, routable fraction f, price ratio r), break-even threshold f*, feasibility bound alpha<1/r

135 HumanEval/ClassEval tasks, 2430 runs across 6 architectures (single strong call, single cheap call, zero-shot router, plain multi-call, OFP-protocol multi-call, mixed-model multi-call); paired bootstrap CIs and Wilcoxon tests per comparison
Protocol overhead directly timed inside the convener (not inferred from end-to-end noise): 7.2ms median per handoff, 0.11% of pipeline wall time
Reproducibility section (S9): full MIT-licensed harness, task builder with pinned dataset hashes, raw run log, discarded runs, analysis scripts released on GitHub
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Closed-form model plus controlled multi-architecture measurement with paired statistics; includes the router/oracle baselines prior multi-agent evaluations typically omit
reproducibilityEvidence: github.com/azettl/coordination-tax-harness (MIT), includes dry-run mode exercising the full harness without model calls
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Narrow claim (decomposition doesn't pay on these 135 code tasks with this model pair) is directly supported by paired statistical tests
candidates.primaryLimitation: Only code-generation tasks tested (executable verification only); both models from one vendor (Anthropic), so protocol-tax and vendor-serving effects cannot be separated
candidates.presentationReason: Notation, derivation, study design and threats-to-validity are all precisely specified with full tables
candidates.reason: Selected: turns 'should we adopt multi-agent decomposition' into a computable break-even question with a directly measured protocol tax, closing the gap that most multi-agent framework evaluations omit (no cheap-single-call or router baseline).

candidates.title: Network Topology Does Not Matter: The Breakdown of Classical Consensus in LLM Populations
candidates.citationVelocity: published 8 days, Semantic Scholar confirms 0 citations
candidates.institution: Sahil Rajesh Dhayalkar; Arizona State University (solo author)
communitySignals: Picked up by GitHub curation list chen742/Awesome_multi-agent-system issue #27 (2026-10-30)
no HF Daily Papers / Papers with Code entry located
credibilityEvidence: Full text read: formal proofs (Props 4.1/4.3, Corollaries 4.2/4.4) that hull-escape and negative realized weight break monotone contraction and conservation
8 instruction-tuned models (0.5B-9B), 73,080 controlled exchanges; credence read deterministically from token-level probabilities (no text parsing)
Three independent measurement instruments (direct operator measurement, real-population validation, extrapolation to 10,000-agent simulation) cross-confirm
Section 5.9/5.10: algebraic connectivity explains almost none of outcome variance at scale; 4 of 8 models (incl. one 7B model) converge to confident false consensus regardless of topology
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Formal proofs paired with large-scale controlled measurement and independent extrapolation validation; first to measure the LLM update operator directly rather than assume classical consensus form
reproducibilityEvidence: Appendix B gives exact prompts, message framings and the credence-readout formula; no code or dataset repository link found in the sections read
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Claim is scoped to the 8 tested models (0.5B-9B); formal proofs and experimental results are mutually consistent
candidates.primaryLimitation: Models tested only up to 9B; frontier closed-source models' token probabilities are usually unavailable, so the same measurement method cannot directly confirm whether they break down the same way
candidates.presentationReason: Three load-bearing assumptions, measurement operator and proofs are all precisely formalized with explicit notation
candidates.reason: Selected: directly measures LLM update behavior rather than assuming it fits classical consensus theory, showing network topology -- the standard design lever for multi-agent debate/discussion systems -- barely affects whether a population converges on a true or false claim.

candidates.title: Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint; full text names a journal submission (Data Science and Management), peer-review status unconfirmed
candidates.citationVelocity: published 4 days; Semantic Scholar 429 rate-limited on 2 retries, inferred near-certain 0 citations given recency
candidates.institution: Mosab Alfaqeeh, Omar Hourani, Muath Hourani (Al-Ahliyya Amman University, Jordan); Hashem Alfaqeeh (Binghamton University, SUNY)
communitySignals: Picked up by community curation bot leisure3318/agents-radar issue #2958 (2026-10-30) as 1 of 14 highlighted papers out of 50 that day
no HF Daily Papers / Papers with Code entry located
credibilityEvidence: Full text read: re-analysis of all 540 released judgments from the Into the Unknown benchmark (9 agents, 15 open research problems) at rubric-criterion level
Manual labeling of 256 numerical claims from 18 submissions with development/confirmation sample split, two annotators, Cohen's kappa=0.89
Deterministic claim-to-evidence checker with operating rules frozen before labeling: 92% precision against human labels (78/85, incl. 27/29 held-out), 23% coverage
Benchmark-wide measurement across 99 submissions; second judge from a different vendor re-grades 30 submissions, preserving agent ranking but with ~2x pass rate
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Development/confirmation sample design with frozen operating rules, two independent annotators, and benchmark-wide + cross-judge validation; authors explicitly scope what the checker does and does not establish
reproducibilityEvidence: github.com/mos3b-faqeeh/agent-integrity-analysis: code, human labels, and derived data released
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The claim (misattribution outweighs fabrication in this benchmark) is backed by layered evidence (judge re-analysis + human labels + deterministic checker + cross-judge check); authors are explicit about single-benchmark scope
candidates.primaryLimitation: Analysis covers only one benchmark (Into the Unknown); the fabrication/misattribution split may differ across other benchmarks or agent populations
candidates.presentationReason: Research questions, checker design, labeling protocol and limitations are all precisely specified with explicit operating points
candidates.reason: Selected: directly bears on the live decision of whether to trust numbers AI research agents report, with a concrete, validated method (claim-to-evidence checking) and the actionable finding that 'not verified' must not be treated as 'false'.
